post.description:
Spends the refresh token and returns a new access token and a new refresh token.

Each refresh token works once. Presenting one that was already rotated is treated as theft:
the whole session is revoked, including the newest token. Clients must therefore serialize
refresh calls: of two concurrent calls with the same token, one succeeds and the other one
ends the session.

422.description: The request is invalid.

401.description: invalid_refresh_token: unknown, expired, revoked or reused refresh token, or the account is suspended.

429.description: rate_limited: too many requests from this client; retry later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the current limit window ends.

post.description:
Revokes the session the refresh token belongs to. No bearer token is needed.

Always 204, so the endpoint cannot be used to test tokens. The access token is not revoked
on the server: it stops working when it expires (`expires_in`).

204.description: Always, whether the token was valid, unknown, expired or revoked.

422.description: The request is invalid.

429.description: rate_limited: too many requests from this client; retry later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the current limit window ends.

post.description:
Sends a verification code by SMS to the number, for the signed-in user.

Always 202 for a valid number, including one already verified by another account (then
nothing is sent). The SMS provider is called after the response, so neither the answer,
its timing nor a provider error tells whether a number is taken; a code that never
arrives surfaces at verify as invalid_code.

202.description: Accepted; a code is on its way by SMS.

422.description: validation_error: not an E.164 number, or a country code that is not allowed.

401.description: invalid_token: missing, invalid or expired access token.

429.description: rate_limited: too many requests from this client; retry later.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset code
post.description:
Emails a 6-digit reset code to the account with this email, if it exists and is active.

Always 202 with no body. The account lookup and the email happen after the response, so
neither the answer nor its timing tells whether the email has an account. A new request
replaces the previous code; a code that never arrives surfaces at reset as invalid_code.

202.description: Always, whether or not an account has this email.

422.description: validation_error: not an email address.

429.description: rate_limited: too many requests from this client; retry later.

post.summary: Reset the password with the code
post.description:
Sets a new password with the emailed code. No bearer token is needed.

The code works once. A success revokes every refresh token of the account, so every
session must log in again; access tokens already issued stop working when they expire.

204.description: The password changed; all sessions ended.

422.description: validation_error: invalid email, a code that is not 6 digits, or password length.

400.description: invalid_code: no code, expired, wrong, already used or out of tries, or no active account with this email.

429.description: rate_limited: too many requests from this client; retry later.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the current limit window ends.

`key` to attach the file to a request, job or profile.

A fixed-price quote: the price in cents, what it includes, the estimated duration and a

duration, the proposed start, when it expires, and the pro's public card.

accepted, where the payment follows; the other quotes stay pending. Calling it again for the

hired: that repeat comes first, then a new acceptance checks the pro (approved, payouts
enabled). The response is the quote as listed, its scope masked; its pro card shows the
pro's current verification.

document, the photo or an internal id (the account, Stripe).

QuoteStatus.title: QuoteStatus
QuoteStatus.description: Internal states (docs/glossary.md). Transitions belong to the state machine (#60).

refresh_token.title: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: The refresh token from the last AuthResponse.

password.title: Password
password.description: Between the server's minimum (setting PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH, 10 by default) and 128 characters. No composition rules.

first_name.title: First Name
first_name.description: 1 to 60 characters after trimming (inner spaces collapsed): letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and periods. No contact details (an email, phone number, website or handle, even spelled out). Both or neither.

last_name.title: Last Name
last_name.description: 1 to 60 characters after trimming (inner spaces collapsed): letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and periods. No contact details (an email, phone number, website or handle, even spelled out). Both or neither.

preferred_date.title: Preferred Date
preferred_date.description: Today or later, as a UTC date.

intake_answers.title: Intake Answers
intake_answers.description: Answers to the category's intake_questions (GET /v1/categories), by question key: an integer, an option value, a list of distinct option values, a boolean or a text, as each question's type says. Empty without a category. A size limit applies; NUL characters and non-finite numbers are refused. Text is stored trimmed.

media_keys.title: Media Keys
media_keys.description: Keys of the caller's own request_media uploads (POST /v1/uploads).

public_code.title: Public Code
public_code.description: The code shown to the customer, e.g. JF-000124.

customer_status.title: Customer Status
customer_status.description: The glossary i18n key the customer sees.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page.

RequestStatus.title: RequestStatus
RequestStatus.description: Internal states (docs/glossary.md). Transitions belong to the state machine (#60).

line1.title: Line1
line1.description: "<number> <street>", or the street alone without a number.

served.title: Served
served.description: Whether an active service area covers the ZIP.

ReverseAddressOut.title: ReverseAddressOut
ReverseAddressOut.description: The US street address at the position, and whether its ZIP is a served area.

ReversePositionIn.title: ReversePositionIn
ReversePositionIn.description:
A device position. Strict: numbers only (no strings or booleans), finite, in range,
and nothing but the two coordinates.

label.title: Label
label.description: The customer's own name for it, e.g. "Home" or "Casa 2".

anyOf.description: Decimal degrees, kept to six decimals.
Decimal degrees, kept to six decimals.

SavedAddressIn.title: SavedAddressIn
SavedAddressIn.description:
A saved address: the address fields, its label, optional coordinates (both or neither)
and whether it becomes the default. The customer's first address is the default anyway.

SavedAddressList.title: SavedAddressList
SavedAddressList.description: The caller's saved addresses: the default first, then the oldest first.

served.title: Served
served.description: True when the ZIP has an active service area; otherwise the app offers the waitlist.

anyOf.description: The customer's own name for it, e.g. "Home" or "Casa 2".
Decimal degrees, kept to six decimals.
Decimal degrees, kept to six decimals.

SavedAddressPatch.title: SavedAddressPatch
SavedAddressPatch.description:
Any subset of the fields. A field left out stays as it is. `line2` sent as null is
cleared; so are `lat` and `lng`, sent as null together. `is_default` can only be true here:
the default moves by making another address the default, never by unsetting one.

key.title: Key

labels.title: Labels
